Hi Mike — thanks again for the intro call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Scope: run a focused evaluation on your payments reconciliation flow (3 canonical prompt families attached) to validate parity against your current proprietary baseline.
2) Metrics: we propose acceptance gates (suggested below) and a small benchmark you can run against a holdout set.
3) Timeline: 2-week trial: 1 week to onboard prompts & data, 1 week to run benchmarks + sync.

Attachments: optipay_eval_promptset_v1.csv (prompt families), redwood_eval_scope.pdf (scope, test plan), benchmark template.

Acceptance gates (initial suggestion):
- Task accuracy: F1 >= 0.85 on reconciliation classification and entity extraction
- Hallucination ceiling: < 2% for no-external-fact answers
- Response quality (human review): >= 4/5 on sampled hits
- P95 latency (in-region): < 800ms for 256-token generation

Model suggestions to trial (open vs baseline comparison):
- Open candidate: LlamaX-13B (8-bit quant) — good cost/latency tradeoff for extraction-heavy prompts
- Open candidate: Mistral-Large-16B (int8) — try for better long-context coherence on multi-step explanations
- Baseline (your current proprietary model): OptiPay-Prod-11B (we'll treat this as the golden baseline for parity analysis)

Evaluation artifacts we will provide: benchmark script + instructions, prompt instrumentation (per-turn scoring), and a template for human review.

Next steps for OptiPay: please confirm we can use the redacted sample dataset (10k rows) and whether legal needs an NDA before we run the trial. If NDA is required, loop in legal and we’ll expedite the SOW.

If that sounds right, I’ll assign Marcus as the SRE/bench lead and Priyom as the prompt-instrumentation owner.
